title: Firefighter Salary NSW: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert a firefighter salary NSW from hourly to annual pay, including casual loading, super, and tax. Use our calculator for a 38-hour week.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, a firefighter's hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours and 52 weeks gives an annual salary, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: How is annual pay calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives a gross annual figure before tax and super. Our calculator assumes 38 hours unless you enter a different weekly hours value.

faqs.q: Does the firefighter salary NSW include casual loading?
faqs.a: The firefighter salary NSW may include casual loading if the role is casual. The Fair Work Commission sets a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. Our calculator has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading to the base rate you enter. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; let the calculator add it.

faqs.q: How is super calculated on top of the salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000, your employer pays an additional $9,600 into your super fund, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Our estimate shows super separately.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Firefighter Salary NSW and Hourly to Annual Conversion

When exploring a **firefighter salary NSW**, you might start with an hourly rate. This guide explains how to convert that hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, including casual loading and superannuation. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool helps you see the full picture.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the calculation is straightforward: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The fortnightly amount is simply weekly pay × 2.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Many firefighters are covered by specific awards that set higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides for each award. Check your award to find the correct base rate. Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual firefighter, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, the minimum casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). Our calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – let the calculator apply it. See our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide for more.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your pay. For a firefighter earning $80,000 annually, the employer contributes an extra $9,600 to super, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how super works.

### Example: Converting a Firefighter Hourly Rate

Suppose a firefighter in NSW has a base hourly rate of $35.00. For a 38-hour week:
- Weekly pay: $35.00 × 38 = $1,330.00
- Fortnightly pay: $1,330.00 × 2 = $2,660.00
- Annual gross: $35.00 × 38 × 52 = $69,160.00

If the role is casual, add 25% loading: $35.00 × 1.25 = $43.75 per hour. Then:
- Weekly: $43.75 × 38 = $1,662.50
- Annual: $43.75 × 38 × 52 = $86,450.00

Super at 12% on the annual gross (if below the cap) adds $10,374.00 on top.

### Tax and Medicare

Tax is based on the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Our estimate uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For the $69,160 annual gross example, tax would be approximately $11,167 plus Medicare $1,383, leaving around $56,610 take-home. See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for more.

### NSW Average Earnings vs Firefighter Salary

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time in New South Wales as $2,108.80 per week (May 2026). This is an average across all industries and occupations, **not the median for a firefighter**. Firefighter salaries vary by experience, location, and award. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page to compare, but remember that averages can be skewed by high earners.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates weekly, fortnightly, annual pay, tax, Medicare, and super. The results are estimates only – they assume no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, salary sacrifice, or HELP repayments. Always consult your employer or a tax professional for your exact situation.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
